parables.title: A fire and the loss of light

passage.arabic:
مَثَلُهُمْ كَمَثَلِ ٱلَّذِى ٱسْتَوْقَدَ نَارًا فَلَمَّآ أَضَآءَتْ مَا حَوْلَهُۥ ذَهَبَ ٱللَّهُ بِنُورِهِمْ وَتَرَكَهُمْ فِى ظُلُمَـٰتٍ لَّا يُبْصِرُونَ
صُمٌّۢ بُكْمٌ عُمْىٌ فَهُمْ لَا يَرْجِعُونَ
passage.translation:
Their likeness is as the likeness of one who kindleth fire, and when it sheddeth its light around him Allah taketh away their light and leaveth them in darkness, where they cannot see,
Deaf, dumb and blind; and they return not.

parables.summary: Al-Tafsir al-Muyassar compares outwardly professed faith followed by rejection with light that is lost in darkness.

nodes.label: Kindled fire
nodes.detail: The opening image provides light around the person.

nodes.label: Light removed
nodes.detail: The passage then describes the removal of light.

nodes.label: Darkness
nodes.detail: The comparison ends with people unable to see.

parables.question: What changes in the image?
parables.reflection: Notice the movement from illumination to darkness. What do the surrounding verses add?

parables.title: Darkness, thunder, and lightning

passage.arabic:
أَوْ كَصَيِّبٍ مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ فِيهِ ظُلُمَـٰتٌ وَرَعْدٌ وَبَرْقٌ يَجْعَلُونَ أَصَـٰبِعَهُمْ فِىٓ ءَاذَانِهِم مِّنَ ٱلصَّوَٰعِقِ حَذَرَ ٱلْمَوْتِ ۚ وَٱللَّهُ مُحِيطٌۢ بِٱلْكَـٰفِرِينَ
يَكَادُ ٱلْبَرْقُ يَخْطَفُ أَبْصَـٰرَهُمْ ۖ كُلَّمَآ أَضَآءَ لَهُم مَّشَوْا۟ فِيهِ وَإِذَآ أَظْلَمَ عَلَيْهِمْ قَامُوا۟ ۚ وَلَوْ شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ لَذَهَبَ بِسَمْعِهِمْ وَأَبْصَـٰرِهِمْ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
passage.translation:
Or like a rainstorm from the sky, wherein is darkness, thunder and the flash of lightning. They thrust their fingers in their ears by reason of the thunder-claps, for fear of death, Allah encompasseth the disbelievers (in His guidance, His omniscience and His omnipotence).
The lightning almost snatcheth away their sight from them. As often as it flasheth forth for them they walk therein, and when it darkeneth against them they stand still. If Allah willed, He could destroy their hearing and their sight. Lo! Allah is able to do all things.

parables.summary: Al-Tafsir al-Muyassar describes a comparison involving fear, intermittent light, and hesitation in response to truth.

nodes.label: Storm
nodes.detail: Rain, darkness, thunder, and lightning form the image.

nodes.label: A flash of light
nodes.detail: They walk when the lightning lights the way.

nodes.label: Darkness returns
nodes.detail: They stand still when darkness falls.

parables.question: When do they walk in the image?
options: When the lightning gives them light.
parables.reflection: Read how movement depends on the flash of light. Keep this observation separate from judging other people.

parables.title: One grain, seven ears

passage.arabic: مَّثَلُ ٱلَّذِينَ يُنفِقُونَ أَمْوَٰلَهُمْ فِى سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ كَمَثَلِ حَبَّةٍ أَنۢبَتَتْ سَبْعَ سَنَابِلَ فِى كُلِّ سُنۢبُلَةٍ مِّا۟ئَةُ حَبَّةٍ ۗ وَٱللَّهُ يُضَـٰعِفُ لِمَن يَشَآءُ ۗ وَٱللَّهُ وَٰسِعٌ عَلِيمٌ
passage.translation: The likeness of those who spend their wealth in Allah's way is as the likeness of a grain which groweth seven ears, in every ear a hundred grains. Allah giveth increase manifold to whom He will. Allah is All-Embracing, All-Knowing.

parables.summary: Al-Tafsir al-Muyassar explains the multiplied grain as a comparison for spending in Allah’s way, with reward according to faith and sincerity.

nodes.label: One grain
nodes.detail: A single grain begins the comparison.

nodes.label: Seven ears
nodes.detail: The grain produces seven ears.

nodes.label: A hundred grains each
nodes.detail: Each ear contains a hundred grains. The verse says Allah multiplies for whom He wills.

parables.question: How many ears does the grain produce?
parables.reflection: The numbers belong to the stated comparison. Do not turn this diagram into a financial return calculator.

parables.title: Soil on a bare rock

passage.arabic: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ لَا تُبْطِلُوا۟ صَدَقَـٰتِكُم بِٱلْمَنِّ وَٱلْأَذَىٰ كَٱلَّذِى يُنفِقُ مَالَهُۥ رِئَآءَ ٱلنَّاسِ وَلَا يُؤْمِنُ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلْيَوْمِ ٱلْـَٔاخِرِ ۖ فَمَثَلُهُۥ كَمَثَلِ صَفْوَانٍ عَلَيْهِ تُرَابٌ فَأَصَابَهُۥ وَابِلٌ فَتَرَكَهُۥ صَلْدًا ۖ لَّا يَقْدِرُونَ عَلَىٰ شَىْءٍ مِّمَّا كَسَبُوا۟ ۗ وَٱللَّهُ لَا يَهْدِى ٱلْقَوْمَ ٱلْكَـٰفِرِينَ
passage.translation: O ye who believe! Render not vain your almsgiving by reproach and injury, like him who spendeth his wealth only to be seen of men and believeth not in Allah and the Last Day. His likeness is as the likeness of a rock whereon is dust of earth; a rainstorm smiteth it, leaving it smooth and bare. They have no control of aught of that which they have gained. Allah guideth not the disbelieving folk.

parables.summary: Al-Tafsir al-Muyassar links the rock washed bare to giving for display and to the loss of reward through reminders and injury.

nodes.label: Rock with soil
nodes.detail: A smooth rock carries a covering of soil.

nodes.label: Heavy rain
nodes.detail: The rain falls on it.

nodes.label: Washed bare
nodes.detail: The rock is left bare. Read the warning about giving at the start of the verse.

parables.question: What does the rain leave behind?
parables.reflection: Compare the opening warning about reminders and injury with the physical image.

parables.title: A garden on high ground

passage.arabic: وَمَثَلُ ٱلَّذِينَ يُنفِقُونَ أَمْوَٰلَهُمُ ٱبْتِغَآءَ مَرْضَاتِ ٱللَّهِ وَتَثْبِيتًا مِّنْ أَنفُسِهِمْ كَمَثَلِ جَنَّةٍۭ بِرَبْوَةٍ أَصَابَهَا وَابِلٌ فَـَٔاتَتْ أُكُلَهَا ضِعْفَيْنِ فَإِن لَّمْ يُصِبْهَا وَابِلٌ فَطَلٌّ ۗ وَٱللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ
passage.translation: And the likeness of those who spend their wealth in search of Allah's pleasure, and for the strengthening of their souls, is as the likeness of a garden on a height. The rainstorm smiteth it and it bringeth forth its fruit twofold. And if the rainstorm smite it not, then the shower. Allah is Seer of what ye do.

parables.summary: Al-Tafsir al-Muyassar compares sincere giving with a fertile elevated garden that benefits from rain or drizzle.

nodes.label: High ground
nodes.detail: A garden stands on elevated ground.

nodes.label: Heavy rain or drizzle
nodes.detail: Both forms of rainfall appear in the verse.

nodes.label: Fruit
nodes.detail: The garden gives its yield. The comparison concerns spending seeking Allah’s pleasure.

parables.question: What can suffice when heavy rain does not fall?
parables.reflection: Read this beside 2:264. What does each image emphasize about the act of giving?

parables.title: A good word and a rooted tree

passage.arabic:
أَلَمْ تَرَ كَيْفَ ضَرَبَ ٱللَّهُ مَثَلًا كَلِمَةً طَيِّبَةً كَشَجَرَةٍ طَيِّبَةٍ أَصْلُهَا ثَابِتٌ وَفَرْعُهَا فِى ٱلسَّمَآءِ
تُؤْتِىٓ أُكُلَهَا كُلَّ حِينٍۭ بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهَا ۗ وَيَضْرِبُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْأَمْثَالَ لِلنَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَذَكَّرُونَ
وَمَثَلُ كَلِمَةٍ خَبِيثَةٍ كَشَجَرَةٍ خَبِيثَةٍ ٱجْتُثَّتْ مِن فَوْقِ ٱلْأَرْضِ مَا لَهَا مِن قَرَارٍ
يُثَبِّتُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ بِٱلْقَوْلِ ٱلثَّابِتِ فِى ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَفِى ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ ۖ وَيُضِلُّ ٱللَّهُ ٱلظَّـٰلِمِينَ ۚ وَيَفْعَلُ ٱللَّهُ مَا يَشَآءُ
passage.translation:
Seest thou not how Allah coineth a similitude: A goodly saying, as a goodly tree, its root set firm, its branches reaching into heaven,
Giving its fruit at every season by permission of its Lord? Allah coineth the similitudes for mankind in order that they may reflect.
And the similitude of a bad saying is as a bad tree, uprooted from upon the earth, possessing no stability.
Allah confirmeth those who believe by a firm saying in the life of the world and in the Hereafter, and Allah sendeth wrong-doers astray. And Allah doeth what He will.

parables.summary: Al-Tafsir al-Muyassar identifies the good word with the declaration of Allah’s oneness and describes faith through the image of rootedness and fruit.

nodes.label: Firm root
nodes.detail: The good tree has a firm root.

nodes.label: Reaching branches
nodes.detail: Its branches reach toward the sky.

nodes.label: Fruit
nodes.detail: It bears fruit by its Lord’s permission. The passage also contrasts an uprooted tree.

parables.question: What distinguishes the good tree?
parables.reflection: Follow both the good and bad tree images in the complete selected passage.

parables.title: Two gardens and a conversation

passage.arabic:
۞ وَٱضْرِبْ لَهُم مَّثَلًا رَّجُلَيْنِ جَعَلْنَا لِأَحَدِهِمَا جَنَّتَيْنِ مِنْ أَعْنَـٰبٍ وَحَفَفْنَـٰهُمَا بِنَخْلٍ وَجَعَلْنَا بَيْنَهُمَا زَرْعًا
كِلْتَا ٱلْجَنَّتَيْنِ ءَاتَتْ أُكُلَهَا وَلَمْ تَظْلِم مِّنْهُ شَيْـًٔا ۚ وَفَجَّرْنَا خِلَـٰلَهُمَا نَهَرًا
وَكَانَ لَهُۥ ثَمَرٌ فَقَالَ لِصَـٰحِبِهِۦ وَهُوَ يُحَاوِرُهُۥٓ أَنَا۠ أَكْثَرُ مِنكَ مَالًا وَأَعَزُّ نَفَرًا
وَدَخَلَ جَنَّتَهُۥ وَهُوَ ظَالِمٌ لِّنَفْسِهِۦ قَالَ مَآ أَظُنُّ أَن تَبِيدَ هَـٰذِهِۦٓ أَبَدًا
وَمَآ أَظُنُّ ٱلسَّاعَةَ قَآئِمَةً وَلَئِن رُّدِدتُّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّى لَأَجِدَنَّ خَيْرًا مِّنْهَا مُنقَلَبًا
قَالَ لَهُۥ صَاحِبُهُۥ وَهُوَ يُحَاوِرُهُۥٓ أَكَفَرْتَ بِٱلَّذِى خَلَقَكَ مِن تُرَابٍ ثُمَّ مِن نُّطْفَةٍ ثُمَّ سَوَّىٰكَ رَجُلًا
لَّـٰكِنَّا۠ هُوَ ٱللَّهُ رَبِّى وَلَآ أُشْرِكُ بِرَبِّىٓ أَحَدًا
وَلَوْلَآ إِذْ دَخَلْتَ جَنَّتَكَ قُلْتَ مَا شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ لَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِٱللَّهِ ۚ إِن تَرَنِ أَنَا۠ أَقَلَّ مِنكَ مَالًا وَوَلَدًا
فَعَسَىٰ رَبِّىٓ أَن يُؤْتِيَنِ خَيْرًا مِّن جَنَّتِكَ وَيُرْسِلَ عَلَيْهَا حُسْبَانًا مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ فَتُصْبِحَ صَعِيدًا زَلَقًا
أَوْ يُصْبِحَ مَآؤُهَا غَوْرًا فَلَن تَسْتَطِيعَ لَهُۥ طَلَبًا
وَأُحِيطَ بِثَمَرِهِۦ فَأَصْبَحَ يُقَلِّبُ كَفَّيْهِ عَلَىٰ مَآ أَنفَقَ فِيهَا وَهِىَ خَاوِيَةٌ عَلَىٰ عُرُوشِهَا وَيَقُولُ يَـٰلَيْتَنِى لَمْ أُشْرِكْ بِرَبِّىٓ أَحَدًا
وَلَمْ تَكُن لَّهُۥ فِئَةٌ يَنصُرُونَهُۥ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ وَمَا كَانَ مُنتَصِرًا
هُنَالِكَ ٱلْوَلَـٰيَةُ لِلَّهِ ٱلْحَقِّ ۚ هُوَ خَيْرٌ ثَوَابًا وَخَيْرٌ عُقْبًا
passage.translation:
Coin for them a similitude: Two men, unto one of whom We had assigned two gardens of grapes, and We had surrounded both with date-palms and had put between them tillage.
Each of the gardens gave its fruit and withheld naught thereof. And We caused a river to gush forth therein.
And he had fruit. And he said unto his comrade, when he spake with him: I am more than thee in wealth, and stronger in respect of men.
And he went into his garden, while he (thus) wronged himself. He said: I think not that all this will ever perish.
I think not that the Hour will ever come, and if indeed I am brought back unto my Lord I surely shall find better than this as a resort.
His comrade, when he (thus) spake with him, exclaimed: Disbelievest thou in Him Who created thee of dust, then of a drop (of seed), and then fashioned thee a man?
But He is Allah, my Lord, and I ascribe unto my Lord no partner.
If only, when thou enteredst thy garden, thou hadst said: That which Allah willeth (will come to pass)! There is no strength save in Allah! Though thou seest me as less than thee in wealth and children,
Yet it may be that my Lord will give me better than thy garden, and will send on it a bolt from heaven, and some morning it will be a smooth hillside,
Or some morning the water thereof will be lost in the earth so that thou canst not make search for it.
And his fruit was beset (with destruction). Then began he to wring his hands for all that he had spent upon it, when (now) it was all ruined on its trellises, and to say: Would that I had ascribed no partner to my Lord!
And he had no troop of men to help him as against Allah, nor could he save himself.
In this case is protection only from Allah, the True, He is Best for reward, and best for consequence.

parables.summary: Al-Tafsir al-Muyassar describes a proud garden owner, his believing companion’s reminder, and the loss of the garden.

nodes.label: Abundance
nodes.detail: Gardens, palms, crops, and a river open the account.

nodes.label: Conversation
nodes.detail: The owner boasts. His companion reminds him of his Creator.

nodes.label: Loss
nodes.detail: The fruit is destroyed, and the owner regrets his earlier association of partners.

parables.question: What does the companion remind the owner about?
parables.reflection: Read each speaker’s words before drawing a conclusion. This diagram summarizes a sequence, not an invented scene.

parables.title: Growth scattered by the wind

passage.arabic: وَٱضْرِبْ لَهُم مَّثَلَ ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا كَمَآءٍ أَنزَلْنَـٰهُ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ فَٱخْتَلَطَ بِهِۦ نَبَاتُ ٱلْأَرْضِ فَأَصْبَحَ هَشِيمًا تَذْرُوهُ ٱلرِّيَـٰحُ ۗ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ مُّقْتَدِرًا
passage.translation: And coin for them the similitude of the life of the world as water which We send down from the sky, and the vegetation of the earth mingleth with it and then becometh dry twigs that the winds scatter. Allah is able to do all things.

parables.summary: Al-Tafsir al-Muyassar connects rain-fed vegetation that becomes scattered dry matter with the beauty and passing nature of worldly life.

nodes.label: Rain
nodes.detail: Water comes down from the sky.

nodes.label: Growth
nodes.detail: The vegetation flourishes through it.

nodes.label: Dry fragments
nodes.detail: The growth becomes dry matter scattered by winds.

parables.question: What scatters the dry growth?
parables.reflection: Notice how quickly the image moves from flourishing vegetation to scattered fragments.

parables.title: A niche, a lamp, and light

passage.arabic: ۞ ٱللَّهُ نُورُ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ ۚ مَثَلُ نُورِهِۦ كَمِشْكَوٰةٍ فِيهَا مِصْبَاحٌ ۖ ٱلْمِصْبَاحُ فِى زُجَاجَةٍ ۖ ٱلزُّجَاجَةُ كَأَنَّهَا كَوْكَبٌ دُرِّىٌّ يُوقَدُ مِن شَجَرَةٍ مُّبَـٰرَكَةٍ زَيْتُونَةٍ لَّا شَرْقِيَّةٍ وَلَا غَرْبِيَّةٍ يَكَادُ زَيْتُهَا يُضِىٓءُ وَلَوْ لَمْ تَمْسَسْهُ نَارٌ ۚ نُّورٌ عَلَىٰ نُورٍ ۗ يَهْدِى ٱللَّهُ لِنُورِهِۦ مَن يَشَآءُ ۚ وَيَضْرِبُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْأَمْثَـٰلَ لِلنَّاسِ ۗ وَٱللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَىْءٍ عَلِيمٌ
passage.translation: Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth. The similitude of His light is as a niche wherein is a lamp. The lamp is in a glass. The glass is as it were a shining star. (This lamp is) kindled from a blessed tree, an olive neither of the East nor of the West, whose oil would almost glow forth (of itself) though no fire touched it. Light upon light. Allah guideth unto His light whom He will. And Allah speaketh to mankind in allegories, for Allah is Knower of all things.

parables.summary: Al-Tafsir al-Muyassar and Al-Jalalayn relate the lamp comparison to guidance in the believer’s heart. This diagram follows the named imagery; it does not depict Allah.

nodes.label: Niche
nodes.detail: The verse names a niche containing a lamp.

nodes.label: Lamp in glass
nodes.detail: The glass is compared with a shining star.

nodes.label: Light upon light
nodes.detail: The verse speaks of oil, light, and Allah guiding whom He wills.

parables.question: Where is the lamp in the comparison?
options: In a niche, enclosed in glass
parables.reflection: Read both cited commentaries. The labels describe the comparison’s imagery, not the divine essence.

parables.title: The spider’s house

passage.arabic: مَثَلُ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّخَذُوا۟ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ أَوْلِيَآءَ كَمَثَلِ ٱلْعَنكَبُوتِ ٱتَّخَذَتْ بَيْتًا ۖ وَإِنَّ أَوْهَنَ ٱلْبُيُوتِ لَبَيْتُ ٱلْعَنكَبُوتِ ۖ لَوْ كَانُوا۟ يَعْلَمُونَ
passage.translation: The likeness of those who choose other patrons than Allah is as the likeness of the spider when she taketh unto herself a house, and lo! the frailest of all houses is the spider's house, if they but knew.

parables.summary: Al-Tafsir al-Muyassar compares reliance on protectors besides Allah with a spider’s house that cannot provide the hoped-for protection.

nodes.label: Seeking protection
nodes.detail: The comparison begins with taking protectors besides Allah.

nodes.label: A spider’s house
nodes.detail: A spider builds a house.

nodes.label: Fragile refuge
nodes.detail: The verse calls it the frailest of houses. This is a comparison about reliance, not a claim about material tensile strength.

parables.question: What is described as the frailest of houses?
parables.reflection: Keep the stated comparison in view rather than turning it into a modern materials-science claim.

parables.title: Conflicting masters and one master

passage.arabic: ضَرَبَ ٱللَّهُ مَثَلًا رَّجُلًا فِيهِ شُرَكَآءُ مُتَشَـٰكِسُونَ وَرَجُلًا سَلَمًا لِّرَجُلٍ هَلْ يَسْتَوِيَانِ مَثَلًا ۚ ٱلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ ۚ بَلْ أَكْثَرُهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ
passage.translation: Allah coineth a similitude: A man in relation to whom are several part-owners, quarrelling, and a man belonging wholly to one man. Are the two equal in similitude? Praise be to Allah! But most of them know not.

parables.summary: Al-Tafsir al-Muyassar contrasts a person claimed by quarrelling partners with one belonging to a single master, explaining a comparison of divided worship and faith.

nodes.label: Quarrelling partners
nodes.detail: One person belongs to partners at odds.

nodes.label: One master
nodes.detail: The other belongs entirely to one master.

nodes.label: A question
nodes.detail: The verse asks whether the two are equal in comparison.

parables.question: How are the partners described?
parables.reflection: Notice the contrast between conflicting demands and a single master, then read the commentary.

parables.title: A flourishing crop that fades

passage.arabic: ٱعْلَمُوٓا۟ أَنَّمَا ٱلْحَيَوٰةُ ٱلدُّنْيَا لَعِبٌ وَلَهْوٌ وَزِينَةٌ وَتَفَاخُرٌۢ بَيْنَكُمْ وَتَكَاثُرٌ فِى ٱلْأَمْوَٰلِ وَٱلْأَوْلَـٰدِ ۖ كَمَثَلِ غَيْثٍ أَعْجَبَ ٱلْكُفَّارَ نَبَاتُهُۥ ثُمَّ يَهِيجُ فَتَرَىٰهُ مُصْفَرًّا ثُمَّ يَكُونُ حُطَـٰمًا ۖ وَفِى ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ عَذَابٌ شَدِيدٌ وَمَغْفِرَةٌ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَرِضْوَٰنٌ ۚ وَمَا ٱلْحَيَوٰةُ ٱلدُّنْيَآ إِلَّا مَتَـٰعُ ٱلْغُرُورِ
passage.translation: Know that the life of the world is only play, and idle talk, and pageantry, and boasting among you, and rivalry in respect of wealth and children; as the likeness of vegetation after rain, whereof the growth is pleasing to the husbandman, but afterward it drieth up and thou seest it turning yellow, then it becometh straw. And in the Hereafter there is grievous punishment, and (also) forgiveness from Allah and His good pleasure, whereas the life of the world is but matter of illusion.

parables.summary: Al-Tafsir al-Muyassar explains the admired crop that turns yellow and crumbles as a comparison for worldly life when the Hereafter is forgotten.

nodes.label: Admired growth
nodes.detail: The rain brings growth that pleases the cultivators.

nodes.label: Yellowing
nodes.detail: The growth later turns yellow.

nodes.label: Dry remnants
nodes.detail: It becomes debris. The verse also names the Hereafter.

parables.question: What color does the growth become?
parables.reflection: Read beyond the crop image to the verse’s final contrast about the Hereafter.

parables.title: A mountain humbled

passage.arabic: لَوْ أَنزَلْنَا هَـٰذَا ٱلْقُرْءَانَ عَلَىٰ جَبَلٍ لَّرَأَيْتَهُۥ خَـٰشِعًا مُّتَصَدِّعًا مِّنْ خَشْيَةِ ٱللَّهِ ۚ وَتِلْكَ ٱلْأَمْثَـٰلُ نَضْرِبُهَا لِلنَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ
passage.translation: If We had caused this Qur'an to descend upon a mountain, thou (O Muhammad) verily hadst seen it humbled, rent asunder by the fear of Allah. Such similitudes coin We for mankind that haply they may reflect.

parables.summary: Al-Tafsir al-Muyassar describes this comparison as an invitation to reflect on the Quran and understand its meanings.

nodes.label: The Quran
nodes.detail: The verse asks us to consider its revelation upon a mountain.

nodes.label: A mighty mountain
nodes.detail: The mountain is described as humbled and split through fear of Allah.

nodes.label: Reflection
nodes.detail: The verse says these comparisons are given so people may reflect.

parables.question: What response is named at the end of the verse?
parables.reflection: Acknowledge the force of the comparison before adding a personal reflection. No mountain event is reconstructed here.

parables.title: Carrying books and bearing responsibility

passage.arabic: مَثَلُ ٱلَّذِينَ حُمِّلُوا۟ ٱلتَّوْرَىٰةَ ثُمَّ لَمْ يَحْمِلُوهَا كَمَثَلِ ٱلْحِمَارِ يَحْمِلُ أَسْفَارًۢا ۚ بِئْسَ مَثَلُ ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا۟ بِـَٔايَـٰتِ ٱللَّهِ ۚ وَٱللَّهُ لَا يَهْدِى ٱلْقَوْمَ ٱلظَّـٰلِمِينَ
passage.translation: The likeness of those who are entrusted with the Law of Moses, yet apply it not, is as the likeness of the ass carrying books. Wretched is the likeness of folk who deny the revelations of Allah. And Allah guideth not wrongdoing folk.

parables.summary: Al-Tafsir al-Muyassar explains the comparison as carrying the Torah without acting on it, like a donkey bearing books without understanding them.

nodes.label: Entrusted with scripture
nodes.detail: The verse identifies those entrusted with the Torah.

nodes.label: A load of books
nodes.detail: The comparison names a donkey carrying books.

nodes.label: Responsibility
nodes.detail: The commentary distinguishes carrying a text from benefiting through acting on it.

parables.question: What is carried in the comparison?
parables.reflection: Read the original context. What distinction does the commentary make between carrying a text and acting on it?

methodology: Fourteen selected comparisons have complete Quran readings, source-attributed commentary summaries, and original three-part reading diagrams. The diagrams organize named imagery and contrasts; they do not depict Allah or prophets, reconstruct events, predict rewards, or replace tafsir. Reflections stay in memory unless explicitly copied or downloaded.
